incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prod/cache service — sustained drop in global hit rate (avg 5m < 55%) — paging threshold crossed. Autopager: paging eng-sre at priority P1. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/cache-hit-rate

mira (oncall): acknowledging. I'm on it, pulling the dashboards now. Noting a few customer errors in the last 3m but not yet widespread.

alex (sre): mira — if the hit-rate is gone we might be seeing a bad eviction storm from the new LRU tweak. Any recent deploys?

mira (oncall): leo, any infra changes in past hour?

leo (infra): We rolled a stealth config to the cache sidecars ~45m ago that changed max_entries per shard. No full deploy, just config reload. I can revert if we think that's culprit.

anya (eng): Confirming I shipped a config to reduce memory pressure on sidecar to avoid OOMs. Noticed evictions increase in canaries but assumed acceptable.

mira (oncall): Ok initial triage: impact scope — 3 customer routes showing 5xx increase, token latency up for low-QPS endpoints. Not full outage, but definitely user-visible for a subset.

alex (sre): Quick mitigation options: 1) revert sidecar config (leo) 2) increase cache memory quota on hot shards 3) temporarily lower pager sensitivity (mute noisy alerts) while we stabilize. I'd roll the revert to canary first then prod.

mira (oncall): Agree. leo, can you revert the config in prod canary shard set now? If canary green, we can promote.

leo (infra): Reverting canary config now. Command I ran: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env ds/cache-sidecar CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=DEFAULT
kubectl -n prod rollout restart ds/cache-sidecar
```
Waiting for canary pods to become Ready.

incident-bot: Deploy started: ds/cache-sidecar revert (canary) — 3 pods.

mira (oncall): canary pods back, initial metrics look like hit-rate for that canary shard climbed from 47% -> 72% in ~4m. No immediate error spike.

anya (eng): That's promising. I'm going to open a short-lived feature-flag rollback in case we need faster revert for remaining shards.

sam (pm): Heads-up: I'm tracking affected customers and pinged two SRE contacts at the larger accounts. We'll prepare a brief postmortem note if this persists.

alex (sre): While we wait to promote, we should mute the flood of low-value alerts and create a tuned alert rule that pages only on persistent multi-shard drops. I'm proposing new alert rule (draft) — see below.

alex (sre): ```
# Prometheus alert: CacheHitRateDrop
- alert: CacheHitRateDrop
  expr: avg_over_time(prod_cache_hit_rate[10m]) < 0.6
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "prod cache hit rate below 60% for 15m"
    runbook: https://internal/runbooks/cache-hit-rate
```

mira (oncall): That 'for: 15m' gives us some breathing room so transient eviction storms don't page. But we still want a fast detect for large customer impact. Maybe add a second rule that pages immediately when multiple shards (>3) have <50% for 5m.

leo (infra): Agree. We can implement shard-level aggregation. Example shard-rule: 
```
- alert: CacheShardMassDrop
  expr: count_over_time((prod_cache_shard_hit_rate < 0.5)[5m]) > 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "multiple cache shards below 50%"
```

ops-runbooks-bot: Note: runbook 'cache-hit-rate' last edited 4 months ago. Suggested edit pending: add 'config-revert' and 'sidecar-restart' quick steps.

mira (oncall): I'm going to mute the noisy alert group for now (@ops-runbooks-bot or whoever owns alerting) — but only for 20m, to avoid missing real critical events.

alex (sre): I'll open an alert-squelch with id: squelch-1987654321 for the "cache-hit-rate-noise" group, expiry 20m. Also creating an incident ticket: INC-1987 with mitigation notes and links to dashboards.

mira (oncall): Can someone add a dashboard panel showing per-customer error delta + per-shard hit rate side-by-side? Right now the global metric hides shard skews.

anya (eng): On it. I'll add a Grafana row: left = per-shard hit rate (heatmap), right = 5m error count by customer. Also adding a trendline for eviction rate. ETA 25m.

leo (infra): Canary looks stable. Proceeding to roll revert to remaining non-zero shards in batches of 5. I'll watch the global dashboards during the rollout.

incident-bot: Rollout progress: 15/20 shard groups reverted, no regressions detected.

mira (oncall): After ~30m post-revert, global hit-rate back to normal band ~75%. Errors dropped to baseline. I recommend: 1) keep new alert rules 2) update runbook to include config-change checklist 3) create per-shard dashboard 4) follow-up postmortem and owners.

alex (sre): Filed followups in INC-1987: ACTIONS: (a) revert config permanently if mem usage acceptable (owner: anya) (b) add per-shard hitrate dashboard + heatmap (owner: anya) (c) add Prometheus shard-level alert (owner: alex) (d) add an automated canary test for eviction spikes on config changes (owner: leo).

sam (pm): I'll coordinate customer comms if we see any downstream reports. For now flagging this as 'near miss' but needs writeup.

mira (oncall): Quick note on alert tuning: We reduced chatter by 80% with the 15m global rule + critical shard rule. Recommend we keep these changes for 72h then reassess in postmortem.

anya (eng): Added dashboard row and pushed to prod. Panels: per-shard hit-rate heatmap, eviction-rate trend, top 10 customers by error delta. Link: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/cache-hitrate

alex (sre): Created Prometheus alert PR: #4521 (includes both global and shard-level rules). Requesting review from infra and eng owners.

leo (infra): Also created quick rollback script and added to runbook: 
```
#!/bin/bash
# quick revert sidecar config
kubectl -n prod set env ds/cache-sidecar CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=DEFAULT
kubectl -n prod rollout restart ds/cache-sidecar
```

mira (oncall): Closing incident as mitigated. Leaving incident ticket open for postmortem and alert tuning followups. If anything pops up, I'll re-open. Thanks everyone for fast response. :thumbsup:

ops-runbooks-bot: Post-incident checklist reminder: assign postmortem owner within 24h, publish summary within 72h.

alex (sre): I'll own the postmortem and sketch a short runbook update. Planning to include graphs, root cause (config change increased eviction churn), mitigation steps, and the alert tuning rationale.

sam (pm): Thanks team. Noting this for the customer-facing summary.

mira (oncall): Final note — action item for SRE: audit recent config changes to sidecar across environments and add a gating canary test to detect eviction surges before rolling to prod.

alex (sre): Noted and added to INC-1987. Closing thread now.
